newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.
newsitem.headline: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.

text.p: By Andrew Bartram*
JORDAN RULES, AUSSIE RULES
Cometh the moment, cometh the man.
In U.S. basketball the moment came for the Chicago Bulls on Friday night when their man Michael Jordan led them to their fifth NBA championship in seven years.
For NORTH MELBOURNE, the moment came on Sunday against ADELAIDE at Football Park. But it was a matter of cometh the men as North fought to a stirring win.
Lesser lights including Brett Allison and Mark Roberts stepped up in the absence of Wayne Carey, who withdrew before the game, and ruckman Corey McKernan, who injured an ankle before halftime.
Allison best illustrated North's resolve when he lined up for his second goal in the tight last quarter. He muttered words of encouragement to himself and then calmly converted the goal.
North will take plenty of beating this year because they are so good in close. Good drivers in heavy traffic as Allan Jeans once said of Garry Ayres.
And their spirit extended to the dressing room after the game with a rousing rendition of their club song.

The Crows had plenty to play for and will, ahem, rue an opportunity lost. A win would have secured ladder leadership following WESTERN BULLDOGS' almost inexplicable loss to PORT ADELAIDE in Melbourne the day before.
The Power trailed by 40 points at quarter time but thereafter kicked 13 goals to four for a two-goal win, their first in Melbourne.
Port are a game clear in seventh place and according to coach John Cahill, a bona fide finals' contender.
ESSENDON slumped to outright second last with their sixth consecutive loss, this time in Perth at the hands of FREMANTLE who kicked their second-highest score en route to a 97-point rout.

HAWTHORN continued their domination over GEELONG at home with a gutsy six-point win at Kardinia Park on Saturday. The Hawks arrested a four-game losing streak with three strong wins in their past three outings and the win was its fourth from its past five Geelong visits.

COLLINGWOOD coach Tony Shaw accepted the blame for his team's fourth straight loss, this time to WEST COAST at Victoria Park on Saturday. Shaw's biggest concern would be the recent form of the Rocca brothers who between them have managed a paltry seven goals in the past three matches.
The EAGLES never lose three in a row and after trailing early, shut down the MAGPIES and kicked away for a 16 point win.

Eagles coach Mick Malthouse called on the AFL to appoint match referees following high farce in Friday night's SYDNEY vs RICHMOND game in which both teams finished a man short after two players were disqualified for incorrectly using the interchange area.
The Swans enjoyed a happy homecoming with an easy 54-point win.

Forecast showers failed to eventuate at Waverley Park during Sunday's clash between ST KILDA and CARLTON but it rained goals as the Saints consolidated their spot in the top eight with an easy win. The final score flattered the Blues who kicked eight consolation goals in the last quarter to add respectability to an otherwise disappointing performance.
BRISBANE recorded their first away win this season thumping MELBOURNE by 85 points at the MCG on Sunday.
An incident involving Melbourne's Alastair Clarkson and Brisbane's Craig Lambert could come under scrutiny when umpires view a replay of the game.
LIONS' coach John Northey will curse the timimg of this weekend's state of origin series just as his team runs into some ominous form. A two-week break could slow their momentum.
*Andrew Bartram is a freelance sports writer who will be writing a regular AFL column for Reuters. Any comments please mark to his attention and send to cybercafe@ca.com.au
